Clarity Coalition: True Value Chain CLEO Shea Carbon
_meta.note: Dual-scenario N-D-C baseline: BAU (traditional women's group production) vs. Serious Shea (eco-processing centre model). N-D-C values derived from TARA technical assessments, women's group survey data, and 2022 final business plan. PROVISIONAL pending full phase-resolved LCA from EP Carbon.

bau.label: BAU (Traditional)
bau.description: Business as usual. Women's groups process shea fruit using traditional fuelwood-based boiling, manual churning, and informal market access. ~6,000 women per province. Income ~USD 150-200/season. GHG ~25 kgCO2e/kg butter.

serious_shea.label: Serious Shea
serious_shea.description: Eco-processing centre model. 50 Collection Sites + 10 Eco-Processing Centres across Burkina Faso. Clean technology (biogas, solar PV), mechanized processing. Income ~USD 450+/season. GHG savings >32,000 tCO2e/yr per processing centre. Backed by AfDB (USD 485k) and World Bank (USD 70k) grants.

phase_meta.name: Shea Parkland Resource Base
phase_meta.transformation: Shea trees (Vitellaria paradoxa) growing in traditional agroforestry parklands across BF savannah zones. ~200 million trees estimated nationally. Average 5-6 kg dry kernel per tree per year. Trees take 15-20 yrs to reach full production; life span 200-300 yrs. Parklands face aging and degradation pressure from fallow loss, plowing, and drought.
phase_meta.actor: Ministry of Environment, local communities, women's groups
phase_meta.sites: Zoundweogo, Cascades, Hauts-Bassins, Boucle du Mouhoun, Est regions
phase_meta.bau_note: Open-access commons. No formal management. Accelerating degradation from fallow loss and tractor tillage.
phase_meta.ss_note: Sensonomic forest management partner engaged. Park mapping and registration for certified supply. Sustainable harvesting training delivered to 300+ women's organizations.

phase_meta.name: Fruit Collection + Kernel Drying
phase_meta.transformation: Seasonal collection of fallen shea fruit by women (May-Aug). De-pulping, boiling or sun-drying to separate nuts from pulp, fermentation/cracking to extract kernels. Kernel moisture reduced to 6-8% for storage. Conversion: 1 kg dry kernel from ~5 kg fresh fruit.
phase_meta.actor: Women's groups (300+ organizations, ~6,000 women in BF)
phase_meta.opacity_reason: Informal smallholder activity; no centralised harvest records. Seasonal and spatially fragmented.
phase_meta.bau_note: Traditional boiling with fuelwood. 15 kg wood consumed per kg butter equivalent. Labour >18 hrs/day. Health risks from smoke.
phase_meta.ss_note: Collection Site infrastructure: solar cookers + steam boilers for boiling; solar-powered motors for de-pulping. Women retain 50% of dried kernels; sell 50% to Serious Shea. 12 collection sites x 720 t/yr = 8,640 t dried kernels/yr (Phase 1).

phase_meta.name: Quality Control + Kernel Storage
phase_meta.transformation: Sorted and graded dried kernels warehoused at collection site or sold to local traders. Key metrics: moisture content (<7%), free fatty acid (FFA) level, colour. FFA rises with poor storage, degrading butter quality and price.
phase_meta.actor: Women's groups, local traders (coxeurs), collection centre managers (SS model)
phase_meta.opacity_reason: BAU storage informal; quality data not systematically recorded. Local trader margin opaque.
phase_meta.bau_note: Informal storage in home or shared facilities. No systematic QC. Kernels sold to travelling traders at 200-300 CFA/kg (USD 0.30-0.46). High post-harvest losses from moisture and pests.
phase_meta.ss_note: Dedicated kernel warehouses at each collection site. Moisture tester + FFA sampling. Traceability via numbered bag IDs. Serious Shea purchases at USD 0.50-0.70/kg (50-100% premium). Organic certification pathway via Ecocert/Soil Association at XOF 2-4M per certified supply.

phase_meta.name: Roasting + Grinding (Paste Production)
phase_meta.transformation: Dried kernels roasted, cooled, crushed and ground to a dark paste (shea paste / shea mass). This is the most energy-intensive step in traditional processing. Paste is the intermediate before water-kneading and butter separation.
phase_meta.bau_note: Manual roasting in clay pots over fuelwood. Manual stone grinding or small diesel mill. Labour intensive: ~8 person-hours per 50 kg kernels. GHG: major fuelwood combustion step.
phase_meta.ss_note: Eco-Processing Centre (1 per 5 collection sites, processing 3,750 t/yr almonds): stainless steel roaster, electric crusher, milling machine driven by solar/biogas. 37 staff per centre (22 processing + manager + logistics).

phase_meta.name: Water Kneading + Butter Separation
phase_meta.transformation: Shea paste kneaded with warm water to separate oil from aqueous fraction. Butter floats and is skimmed. Boiled to evaporate water and kill microbes. Shea cake (residual protein mass) and process water are waste streams. Conversion: ~3.75 kg kernels per 1 kg butter.
phase_meta.bau_note: Open water basins, wood-fired boiling. Significant water use (estimated 30-50 L per kg butter). Butter yield 25-28% of kernel weight. Shea cake discarded or used as fertilizer ad hoc.
phase_meta.ss_note: Stainless steel barrate (mechanical churner). Recycled process water. Biogas from fruit pulp waste reduces fuelwood to zero. Shea cake directed to composting + potential biogas feedstock. Butter yield 26-28%. Each processing centre: 3,750 t kernels in → 1,000 t butter out.

phase_meta.name: Packaging + Export Preparation
phase_meta.transformation: Raw (unrefined) shea butter filled into drums or IBC containers. Quality documentation prepared: FFA %, moisture %, colour grade, country of origin. For cosmetic-grade: cold-pressed variants selected. For food-grade: additional fractionation to separate shea stearin (higher melting point, used in CBE) and shea olein.
phase_meta.actor: Serious Shea operations team, export brokers
phase_meta.bau_note: Butter sold locally in gourds or plastic bags at 500-1,000 CFA/kg (USD 0.76-1.52). No export documentation. No quality certification. No access to international buyers.
phase_meta.ss_note: Target specifications: melting point 32°C preferred by cosmetic buyers; FFA <1.5%. Export drums and IBCs. Buyers confirmed: Berg & Schmidt, L'Occitane, Lamotte Oils, Bunge Loders Crocklaan. Phase 1 output: 3,206 t/yr butter for export.

phase_meta.name: Certification + Carbon Credit Registration
phase_meta.transformation: Product certification for premium cosmetic markets (NaTrue, Cosmos, Ecocert organic, FairWild). Carbon credits generated from: (a) fuel substitution (fuelwood avoided), (b) biochar/residual carbon in soil, (c) shea parkland protection and reforestation. Credits registered on voluntary carbon market.
phase_meta.actor: Ecocert, Soil Association, REDD+ assessors, World Bank TerrAfrica, voluntary carbon registries
phase_meta.bau_note: No certifications. No carbon accounting. No REDD+ participation.
phase_meta.ss_note: World Bank USD 70k REDD+ assessment completed. Each centre saves >32,000 tCO2e/yr; 10 centres = 320,000+ tCO2e/yr total avoided emissions. Carbon sequestration in protected shea parklands: 49-215 tCO2e/ha (Côte d'Ivoire reference, BF values similar). Organic certification: XOF 2-4M per certified supply.

phase_meta.name: Market Delivery + Women's Income Return
phase_meta.transformation: Certified shea butter exported to international cosmetics and food buyers. Carbon credits sold on voluntary carbon market. Women's groups receive premium kernel price, 50% of retained kernels for own processing, and 10% profit-share from community fund.
phase_meta.actor: International cosmetics manufacturers, food/confectionery processors, voluntary carbon market, community fund
phase_meta.bau_note: Women sell to local market traders at depressed prices. No access to international pricing. No profit share. Effective price for women: USD 0.76-1.52/kg butter equivalent.
phase_meta.ss_note: Export price tiers: Cosmetic/Organic USD 3.50/kg, Cosmetic/Standard USD 2.50/kg, Food/Confectionery USD 2.00/kg. Community fund 10% profit share = ~USD 300k/yr for schools and clinics. Women's income per season: min USD 450 (vs. ~USD 150-200 BAU).

processing_cluster.description: Each cluster = 5 collection sites + 1 eco-processing centre

shea_pulp.treatment_ss: Biogas feedstock in biodigester at processing centre
shea_pulp.carbon_value: Biogas displaces fuelwood; counts toward avoided emissions credit

shea_cake.treatment_ss: Compost + potential biogas co-feedstock; organic fertilizer returned to parklands

nut_shells.treatment_ss: Syngas generation in processing centre; displaces grid/diesel

process_water.treatment_ss: Recycled within centre; reduces freshwater draw

parkland_co2_sequestration_t_ha.reference: Alui et al., Côte d'Ivoire, 2020; Ferrasol and Cambisol soils

carbon_science.redd_plus_assessment: World Bank TerrAfrica grant USD 70k; assessment complete 2022
